CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath that occurs with mild exercise or walking, such as walking up her driveway. She reports associated palpitations. She notes the shortness of breath has been happening more often lately. She is uncertain if it is related to her chronic back pain. She reports increased exercise recently to address weight gain from COVID-19. She previously smoked two packs per day but has reduced to approximately one cigarette per day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No other issues reported. Denies fever, chills, or other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Depression
- Chronic back pain
- Smoking history (2 packs per day previously, now reduced to approximately 1 cigarette per day)

MEDICATIONS
- Effexor for depression
- Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
The patient is a smoker, currently smoking approximately one cigarette per day, down from two packs per day. She exercises more recently to manage weight. She has not established a consistent yoga practice despite previous discussion.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs and general examination normal. Lung examination reveals mild wheezes in all lung fields. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests show evidence of possible asthma or COPD. Chest X-ray demonstrates flattened diaphragm consistent with COPD.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Patient prescribed Combivent inhaler two puffs twice daily to help open airways. Albuterol inhaler two puffs as needed for acute shortness of breath. Prednisone taper pack prescribed. Depression stable on current Effexor therapy; continue current dose. Continue Gabapentin for chronic back pain management. Encouraged to continue exercise and consider yoga for depression and back pain management.
